items.article_search_text: Kimi Antonelli insists the Formula 1 title race is “not over” as he takes a vast 81-point lead into this week’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Antonelli sounds cautious as he heads Kimi Antonelli insists the Formula 1 title race is “not over” as he takes a vast 81-point lead into this week’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Antonelli sounds cautious as he heads to a track where Oscar Piastri's title run began to fall apart a year ago with an opening-lap crash while the Australian led the standings. Still, Antonelli’s lead is more than double the biggest advantage Piastri had last year. The race is held on a Saturday to make way for a national day of remembrance on Sunday. That means Thursday practice and Friday qualifying. Kimi Antonelli insists the Formula 1 title race is “not over” as he takes a vast 81-point lead into this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.It looks as good as over, but Baku has sprung surprises before.A year ago, that was where Oscar Piastri's title shot began to fall apart. The Australian was leading the standings when he almost stalled on the grid, dropped to last and crashed, all in the space of about a minute on the opening lap.That kicked off a run of six races without a podium finish for Piastri, who had to watch the title race become a fight between eventual champion Lando Norris and Max Verstappen.Antonelli is sounding cautious as he aims to become F1's youngest-ever champion.“Until you cross that finish line, it’s not over. It’s like tennis, one point at a time, here one race at a time," he said. “The sooner it’s over, the better it is. Still a long way and it’s not going to be easy. It’s going to be intense but I’m ready to give my best and to keep having fun.”There are key differences this year. For one thing, Antonelli’s lead is more than double the biggest advantage Piastri had last year. He’s coming off back-to-back wins, not the team orders controversy which was dogging Piastri and Norris a year ago.As for Piastri, he says it's “love-hate in some ways” as he returns to a venue where he won in 2024 and endured a nightmare 2025.“I think probably my best race ever has been at this track and probably my worst race ever has been at this track, so always eventful,” Piastri said.Antonelli's title rivals need to bounce backThe three British drivers behind Antonelli are all trying to recover from disappointing races at the Spanish Grand Prix two weeks ago.Antonelli's teammate George Russell all but ruled himself out of the title race after an uncompetitive run to fifth in Madrid, while Lando Norris was left ruing a badly-timed virtual safety car which cost him the win. Lewis Hamilton retired, making it five races off the podium for the Ferrari driver.“I’m going to keep fighting every single race until it’s mathematically impossible, but it doesn’t change how I go about my job," Russell said Wednesday. "There’s obviously a huge deficit, but it’s not even really a consideration right now.”Red Bull's double bet on Isack HadjarRed Bull is backing Isack Hadjar's health and his potential in the hope the young French driver develops into one of F1's top talents.Hadjar returns for Baku despite saying he still feels pain from the wrist fracture which ruled him out of the last three races. And he has a contract extension to partner Max Verstappen for 2027, too.Wrist injuries can have long-term consequences. Lance Stroll rushed back from wrist fractures sustained in a preseason cycling crash in 2023 but ended up missing a race after all in 2025 when he needed a follow-up operation to deal with lingering pain.A rare Saturday race amid broader F1 schedule uncertaintyIt's an unusual race week in a very unusual F1 season, as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix is held on a Saturday to make way for a national day of remembrance on Sunday. That means Thursday practice and Friday qualifying.This starts a run of three races in three weeks because of the extra round next week in Malaysia, still carrying branding of the called-off Bahrain Grand Prix.See AP’s full auto racing coverage here Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Italy walks through the paddock ahead of the Azerbaijan F1 Grand Prix, in Baku, Azerbaijan, Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. items.article_search_text: McLaren driver Oscar Piastri said at a press conference in Baku ahead of the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix that he is looking forward to racing at the Baku City Circuit and believes the track offers a unique challenge. Piastri noted that the circuit requires confidence from drivers and combines a large number of corners with the characteristics of a street track. He added that racing in Baku is always exciting and expressed hope that this year's weekend would be more successful for McLaren. The Australian driver also spoke about the team's performance at the previous race weekend. He said McLaren had sufficient pace but was not always able to show its full potential. Piastri added that the team has been making progress and testing several upgrades, some of which have worked while others have not produced the expected results. He stressed that McLaren will continue working on the car and does not intend to stop developing it as the season progresses. The 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be held at the Baku City Circuit from September 24 to 26. The weekend will feature Free Practice 1 and 2 on Thursday, followed by Free Practice 3 and qualifying on Friday, while the 51-lap Grand Prix will take place on Saturday at 15:00 local time. items.article_search_text: FORMULA1 Ətraflı oxu Oscar Piastri on Baku circuit: McLaren driver Oscar Piastri has shared his mindset heading into the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, as well as how he and the team are working to improve their performance this season. Offsideplus.az reports that the Australian driver emphasized that they are mobilizing all their efforts to make progress: "We've thrown everything into making progress and pushing forward. I think the team reacted really well to the situation, trying to fix everything as quickly as possible. I feel great support within the team. This year's cars are very different from what we worked with before — many solutions that used to work are now ineffective. It's not simple here: you can't just find one direction and rely on it every time, you have to keep looking for new solutions." The McLaren driver also shared his thoughts on the Baku circuit: "My feelings towards the Azerbaijan Grand Prix track are mixed, so to speak. I've had both my best and worst Formula 1 races on this circuit. But it really is an interesting track — I hope this race goes more according to the scenario of the 2024 edition." items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission about driving the 2026 Formula 1 cars, stating that the AI reduces his Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission about driving the 2026 F1 cars, stating that the AI reduces his input at points when out on track. Motorsport Week is an independent, FIA accredited motorsport website delivering the latest Formula 1, Formula E, GP2, GP3, WEC, IndyCar, Nascar, Formula 3, WRC, WRX, DTM, IMSA and MotoGP news and results. Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission about driving the 2026 Formula 1 cars, stating that the AI reduces his input at points when out on track. Piastri is enduring a challenging season, struggling to get to grips with the new generation of car, yet to win a race in 2026. The Australian has been one of the more quieter drivers in giving his verdict on the cars, which feature a near 50:50 split in electrical and internal combustion power. But he has made an damning admission over the computer systems onboard the cars, which actively learns the circuit and how to deploy the battery during a lap. "Sometimes, yes," Piastri said to media, including Motorsport Week, if he "felt like a passenger of the AI systems". "At a track like Spa or a track like Silverstone, it’s going to be worse. At the Hungaroring or Zandvoort, I really don’t expect there to be many problems at all with that kind of thing, because the straights are so much shorter, so even if there are differences, they should be a lot less. "But the principle of driving a race car that loses effectively half of its power before the end of the straight is hard to get your head around sometimes. Oscar Piastri has made a damning admission over the AI in the current generation of F1 cars Oscar Piastri details AI issues Elaborating on his point, Piastri detailed the radical way the car learns the sectors of the legendary Spa circuit. "Even in Spa, a lot of the middle sector we were doing it just on the combustion engine, with no battery assistance at all, which is a weird feeling in itself, having some corners with a certain amount of power and others with full power. "I think Spa was particularly frustrating, not just for me but for quite a lot of others, because those small differences in the code and what the engines did made quite a big difference in lap time. "Especially at the front of the field, I think there were still only nine hundredths or something separating four positions, and there were definitely more than nine hundredths on the table for quite a few drivers from things they could not control." Piastri's feedback on the car's AI systems highlights the journey F1 faces with these regulations. For a driver to feel like a passenger is not a sentiment many will want to experience. items.article_search_text: McLaren F1 star Oscar Piastri teamed up with Kevin Pietersen on The Switch to showcase his cricket skills against a 100 mph bowling machine. have i ever watched a cricket game before? no do i know any cricket rules? Oscar Piastri playing cricket wasn’t on anyone’s bingo card. In a surprising crossover that has fans talking, the McLaren Formula 1 driver recently traded the racetrack for the crease.The Australian star took on a high-speed cricket challenge on his YouTube series, The Switch, hosted by former England batsman Kevin Pietersen. Filmed around mid-August 2026, the off-track session used a bowling machine to push deliveries up toward the 100mph mark just for fun.Now, F1 fans are left wondering if he can actually play the game and how he managed to handle those intense deliveries. Let's see exactly what went down!Piastri is still fully committed to McLaren and his Formula 1 career. The cricket session was just a fun, light-hearted guest appearance on Kevin Pietersen’s YouTube series, , reportedly per .Reports confirm that it was strictly a one-off challenge with a bowling machine, rather than any sort of career change or exit from the F1 grid. The McLaren driver is still racing in the 2026 season with his usual car number, 81.The Melbourne-born driver actually grew up playing junior cricket, mostly as a bowler, along with Australian Rules football before he shifted his focus entirely to karting and racing.He’s often spoken about his genuine love for the game, reportedly even heading out to watch matches like the Melbourne Test, and is good friends with players like Mitchell Starc. During the challenge, he took on deliveries from a bowling machine that started at 51 mph, playing with three “lives” as the speed progressively cranked up.Piastri managed to handle deliveries all the way up to 81 mph. Starting at 51 mph and using his three allotted lives, he steadily worked his way through the different speeds on the bowling machine, reportedly reaching 81 mph at his final attempt.That final 81 mph figure happened to perfectly match his Formula 1 race number, adding a fun coincidence to the session. Even though he didn't quite hit the maximum 100 mph target, it was still a really impressive performance for someone who isn't a professional cricketer.Clocking in at 81 mph actually puts Piastri second on challenge leaderboard. The ranking reportedly has Bollywood actor Suniel Shetty holding onto the top spot with a higher speed of around 91 to 92 mph, while tennis star Andy Murray finished just behind at 79 mph.This places the F1 driver ahead of quite a few other high-profile guests who have taken on the exact same progressive speed bowling machine test.One user on Reddit wrote, “First we had Max vs 100 drivers. Now it's Oscar vs 100 mph ball. Wonder what's next for the vs 100 series.”Another mentioned, “His first instinct is to go defensive. That's how you know he's an Aussie batter.” A third joked, “I laughed so hard when he left the ball.” Another added, “Australian player defaults to Test match mode, as per usual.”For Piastri, the cricket challenge was another reminder that his sporting talent stretches far beyond the Formula 1 circuit.

items.title: Stella: “Piastri Drives Thinking Too Much and That Holds Him Back”

items.article_search_text: The McLaren boss attributes the Australian's lack of pace to excessive reflection behind the wheel of the MCL40. The team has designed a plan for him to recover his fluency and fight for the podium again in the final stretch of the season. Andrea Stella has identified the source of Oscar Piastri [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-describes-spanish-gp-as-painful-after-challenging-f1-outing]'s problems. The McLaren boss considers that the Australian driver is "thinking too much" while driving the MCL40, which prevents him from extracting the full potential of the car and is costing him valuable tenths in qualifying and races: "I think with Oscar we need to qualify better and be closer to the podium positions from the start, there are several circumstances over which we need more control. We need to execute the work better and at the same time achieve greater synchrony between Oscar and the MCL40, since he still drives thinking too much" declared Stella in Madrid. The Italian executive's diagnosis points to an adaptation problem. Piastri, who in 2025 had stood out for his ability to maintain great speed in fast corners, has not been able to consistently reproduce that style with the current generation of cars, the reduction in downforce and narrower tires have altered the behavior of the cars, reducing available grip and demanding a different driving approach. Oscar Piastri describes Spanish GP as “painful” after challenging F1 outing [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/60f26e36-1416-4168-8752-9508c5914746.jpeg] Oscar Piastri describes Spanish GP as “painful” after challenging F1 outing The Australian finished eighth after suffering front wing damage on the first lap from contact with Russell. The bad timing of the Virtual Safety Car and a complicated qualifying session hampered his race at Madring. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-describes-spanish-gp-as-painful-after-challenging-f1-outing] For Piastri that adaptation process is proving slower than expected, Stella explained how this excess reflection directly affects performance: "When you drive thinking too much everything becomes slower, you become slower as a driver when deciding what to do and consequently, you do slower laps" he noted. The McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]boss trusts that the team can reverse the situation. "The plan is very clear in terms of what we need to improve and I hope we get past this seeing a stronger Piastri in the final part of the year" he added. The Monza case is a representative example of Piastri's season, the Australian qualified third but a penalty for impeding another driver dropped him to sixth place on the grid, ruining his podium chances: "In Monza, he was third in qualifying but we ended up starting sixth due to a penalty. There are several circumstances over which we need more control" lamented Stella. F1 Stock Watch: Who Gained and Lost More After Madrid? [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/b429bb20-8779-402e-811d-c0b69c9373bc.jpeg] F1 Stock Watch: Who Gained and Lost More After Madrid? Kimi Antonelli's stock is through the roof, while Carlos Sainz Jr's hometown flop will hurt him. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-stock-watch-who-gained-and-lost-more-after-madrid] The figures reflect the gap between McLaren's two drivers, Piastri has 120 points and occupies seventh place in the championship, with two podiums and no wins. Lando Norris, for his part, is fourth with 186 points, two wins and five podiums. The 66 point difference between them is a reflection of the Australian's lack of consistency, who has not managed to find the consistency needed to fight for the title. McLaren has established a strategy to recover Piastri's performance in the second half of the season. The goal is to achieve greater synchrony between the driver and the car so that Piastri can drive more instinctively and less analytically, the team trusts that with more adaptation time and specific work on the MCL40's setup, the Australian can recover the fluency that led him to shine in previous seasons. Formula 1 [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1] will return to action in Baku, where Piastri will have a new opportunity to demonstrate that McLaren's recovery plan is producing results. The Australian knows time is pressing and that every race is a chance to recover the confidence and pace that made him one of the most promising drivers on the grid.
